themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions in Fordham/University Heights have spiked dramatically THIS WEEK with 38 complaints compared to a 5.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 607% increase (z-score: 12.81)—suggesting rapid deterioration in road quality that requires immediate investigation into what triggered this sudden infrastructure failure.
evidence: 38 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly baseline (607% spike)
Z-score of 12.81 indicates statistically extreme deviation
176 total street condition complaints over past 90 days concentrated in this acute spike
reporting_angles: Interview DOT about whether potholes, flooding, or other specific street damage triggered the spike—was there recent weather, construction, or infrastructure failure?
Map complaint locations to identify whether the problem is localized to specific corridors (near transit, commercial areas, residential blocks) or district-wide

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints have surged to 5 reports THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1900% spike (z-score: 10.97)—raising concerns about sanitation response capacity, potential disease vectors, or environmental conditions driving animal mortality in the district.
evidence: 5 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% spike)
Z-score of 10.97 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Timing coincides with street condition spike, suggesting possible correlation
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation and Animal Care & Control: are they aware of the spike? Is there disease outbreak concern? What's causing elevated mortality?
Interview residents about where bodies are appearing (parks, streets, waterfront) and whether they've noticed behavioral changes in local wildlife

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness-related encampment complaints have jumped to 12 reports THIS WEEK from a 1.4 weekly average—a 773% increase (z-score: 10.71)—indicating either rapid growth in unsheltered populations or concentrated new encampments that may strain city services and community resources.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (773% spike)
Aligns with repeated community board budget requests for public health and social services programs
reporting_angles: Map THIS WEEK's 12 encampment locations: are they concentrated in specific parks, transit nodes, or neighborhoods, or dispersed throughout CD 205?

Interview NYC Department of Homeless Services, local nonprofits, and community board about whether they've observed this spike and what triggered it—seasonal factors, shelter closures, or service changes?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped to 26 reports LAST WEEK from a 5.6 weekly average—a 362% spike (z-score: 11.33)—suggesting either increased traffic congestion, illegal street racing, or vehicles without proper mufflers creating quality-of-life degradation for residents.
evidence: 26 vehicle noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly average (362% spike)
Z-score of 11.33 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Complements street noise spike (153 complaints last week vs. 22.6 avg, 576% increase) suggesting broader traffic or street activity problem
reporting_angles: Report on whether NYPD has increased traffic enforcement or received community complaints about specific high-traffic corridors or racing hotspots in Fordham/University Heights
Interview residents about timing of noise complaints—is it weekends, late night, specific routes? Could point to organized street racing or construction activity

themes_detail.label: Sanitation System Strain
themes_detail.summary: Dirty conditions complaints spiked to 39 reports LAST WEEK from an 11.0 weekly average—a 254% increase (z-score: 7.23)—coupled with the community board's repeated multi-year budget request for more sanitation trucks, suggesting the district's waste management infrastructure is inadequate to handle current volume.
evidence: 39 dirty condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 11.0 weekly baseline (254% spike)
Community board has filed the same 'provide more sanitation trucks' budget request year-over-year—chronic, unresolved need
reporting_angles: FOIA request to NYC Sanitation: what is the truck allocation and collection schedule for CD 205? Has it changed recently or is it inadequate for demand?
Interview Sanitation union and district coordinator about staffing, truck breakdowns, or service reductions that might explain the spike in dirty complaints
